app_records.description: Wire 3.2: Paykit's member of an app record, protocols.paykit, as a Paykit reader reads it. Each record is the shop app record of the Switch set's documents.json with its paykit member changed or removed (and, last of refused, expires_at null too), signed again with the shop's signing key; the signatures verify. The switch takes every one, since it checks only the form of protocols (Switch wire 3.2). accepted are records a Paykit reader takes, the first the shop's record as it is; reads is what the reader takes from each: the Payment Endpoint Identifiers of capabilities.endpoint_identifiers, and the public endpoints. A missing or null paykit member, capabilities, endpoint_identifiers or public_endpoints reads as empty, and unknown members are ignored. refused are records Paykit's readers refuse, though the switch takes them (switch_accepts): a capabilities or public_endpoints that isn't an object, an endpoint_identifiers that isn't an array of strings, a payload that isn't a string, and public endpoints with expires_at null. protocols and expires_at are the record's as signed. reason is the prototype's wording at a Paykit reader.

certificate_rejections.description: Wire 3.1: certificates whose permissions are well formed but aren't exactly the list Paykit's table derives from their scopes (paykit_permissions). Each is the wallet certificate of the Switch set's documents.json with scopes and permissions changed, signed by alice's identity key; the signatures verify. The switch takes them and enforces exactly that list (switch_accepts), while Paykit's verifiers, apps and payers, refuse them. The lists that aren't well formed, which every verifier refuses, are the Switch set's permission_rejections. reason is the prototype's wording at a Paykit verifier.

The certificates are the Switch set's documents.json certificates with scopes or permissions changed, and the app records its shop app record with its Paykit member changed.

labelled_scope_rejections.description: Wire 3.1, Switch wire 3.1: certificates every verifier refuses for their labelled selling scopes request:<label> (a label is 1 to 32 characters of a-z, 0-9 and -, starting with a letter or digit; at most 8 per certificate; never beside plain request, which covers every label). Each is the hosted certificate with scopes changed and permissions derived from them, signed by bob's identity key; reason is the prototype's wording. switch_accepts says whether the switch takes it: its generic scope rule refuses a label of 33 characters, one that isn't valid, an empty one and plain request beside request:shop1, while nine labels break only Paykit's bound of 8.
